located within the Los Angeles, California fashion district (referred to hereafter as the
“Los Angeles Fashion District GTO”).12 The Los Angeles Fashion District GTO applied
to certain specified types of “Covered Businesses,” including “perfume stores,” in a
“Covered Geographic Area” that encompassed A&S’s Fine Fragrance location at 501
East Olympic Boulevard.13

course of its trade or business, received currency in excess of $3,000 in one transaction
or two or more related transactions in a 24-hour period, to report such transactions
electronically to FinCEN.14 The Los Angeles Fashion District GTO was effective from
October 9, 2014 through April 6, 2015.

statutory.answer: Yes, the conduct described falls within 31 U.S.C. § 5324(a)(3) prohibits structuring.
statutory.label: entailment
statutory.reasoning: Under 31 U.S.C. § 5324(a)(3), it is unlawful to structure transactions to evade reporting requirements. The fact pattern shows multiple cash deposits just below the reporting threshold: $9,023.77 on 2026-04-22, $53,982.83 on 2026-04-03, $91,100.08 on 2026-02-19, and $91,095.77 on 2026-04-03. While the entity is a cash-intensive grocery store, the aggregation of these cash amounts across different dates suggests an attempt to avoid triggering Currency Transaction Reports (CTRs). The presence of these sub-threshold cash deposits is sufficient to indicate potential structuring under the statute.
